frequency_question: What fraction of expiring bilateral water treaties between federal republics and neighbors fail to achieve renewal due to internal structural friction?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral water-sharing treaties between sovereign states where at least one party is a federal system with sub-national veto actors (such as downstream provinces/states), reaching a mandatory renewal or extension clause.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty (Permanent, but friction points in 1978 Salal / 2015 Kishenganga)
1944 U.S.-Mexico Water Treaty (Colorado/Rio Grande supplementary protocols)
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase agreements (Treaty extensions)
Senegal River Basin Charter and associated protocols
Columbia River Treaty regime modifications and renegotiation framework

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named; believed roughly 8-9 in total globally for this specific structural class.
known_gaps: Excludes minor unratified memorandums of understanding and non-federal unitary state treaties.
skeleton: Total major interstate water treaty renewal/extension events meeting federal structural criteria since 1974 divided by those that successfully renewed.
multiplier: 6 successes out of 6 documented comparable federal-neighbor treaty renewal/extension cycles.
validity_reason: Treaty structures and international water law norms evolve slowly over multi-decade cycles; the structural baseline remains stable through the end of the decade.
